display.title: Episode 551: The Stargazer and the Snake: Tzedakah Saves from Death
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi marks program number 551, leads Tehillim and Shema with a Brooklyn class, and tells how a piece of bread given to a starving man saved a young traveler from a snake.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi celebrates program number 551 of Tzivos Hashem on the Air, which began more than eleven years earlier and whose audience has grown since the move to Sunday evenings, and prays to continue until it broadcasts from Yerushalayim with Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march the children say Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery, followed by an advertisement. A class from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: a stargazer who cannot get anyone in the marketplace to believe him predicts that a young man walking into the forest will not come back alive. When the young man returns cheerful, the crowd laughs, but the stargazer asks what happened. The young man had shared his bread with a starving old man, and when he opened his sack a snake jumped out. Uncle Yossi explains, as Shlomo HaMelech wrote, that tzedakah saves from death and brings Hashem's blessings. After a grocery advertisement, Uncle Yossi reads a listener's letter about the whole family marching with the Hakochainik, and closes with Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Tzedakah is so powerful it can save a life; Jews look to the Torah, not the stars, for answers.
